title: Check yourself: The conversation state the client keeps, and a conversation client

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A chat client appends each user turn to its history before calling the API. After a night of occasional 529 errors, some conversations answer oddly, and their stored history shows two user turns in a row. What is the best fix?

options.text: Retry every failed call forever so that no turn is ever left without its answer by morning
options.says: Ruled out because a retry is a separate decision, and the page says the retry "will send a different conversation from the one the user saw" if the history is damaged.

options.text: Take that entry out again whenever the call raises, so that only whole exchanges are kept
options.says: The rule is to "commit a turn only when the whole exchange succeeded", which means removing the user turn on any failure.

options.text: Merge any two consecutive user turns into one when the history is saved
options.says: Ruled out because a merge hides the damage while "the next request contains two user turns in a row" in the very same way, and a question that never got an answer stays in the history.

options.text: Store only the assistant turns, which are the ones that the model produced
options.says: Ruled out because "the whole list goes in every request", and a list without user turns is not a conversation.

questions.stem: A product team notices that a support conversation of 40 turns costs far more than four conversations of 10 turns, although the total number of questions is the same. What explains it?

options.text: The system prompt is repeated once for every question, so it dominates the bill
options.says: Ruled out because the system prompt is the same size on every turn, and the page says "every turn resends everything before it", so the history is what grows.

options.text: Long conversations are charged at a higher price for each output token that is produced
options.says: Ruled out because nothing on the page prices long conversations differently, and the growth comes from input: "every turn resends everything before it".

options.text: The model writes longer replies as a conversation grows, and the replies dominate the bill in the end
options.says: Ruled out because "turn n sends about 200 n input tokens", which is growth in input and not in replies.

options.text: Each call repeats the earlier exchanges, so the input bill grows with the square of the length
options.says: The page says "the input cost of a conversation grows with the square of its length", because each turn resends everything before it.
